why: Cycle 9 of the expression area (docs/v3/cycles/expression-9.md) ran six native cases that had never run, again with no referenced case because TuffUI published nothing after `f31ea2b`. Round-0 median 79, minimum 67, two cases passing at once (n34 82, n35 85), no P1 and 10 P2; on the F and K items the median was 83.5, the best of nine cycles. 48 of 76 lost points were `skill`, 25 `primitive` and 3 `rubric`. Repair rounds lifted the median by only 2 points (on the F and K items it fell 1.5), so hypothesis 1 met its kill clause; the two cases that never passed (n33, n36) are pages of tables whose builders named kit limits in every round. Its fix rows (v3-expr-9-contract, v3-expr-9-kit-fixes, v3-expr-9-skill, v3-expr-9-rubric) add a list row that joins a chart's focus across grains and a declared table skeleton row count behind a Spec; fix the loading height at 390, label keeping, refLine labels at 390, clamped-mark values, dim strength and phone cards in the kit; teach linked parts without a chart, age columns as meters, the answer on the mark, targets, colour for HTML marks, the fact count and table anatomy; and give X3 and X4 one reading on a page with no chart. This cycle measures again on six cases that have never run, and re-measures hypothesis 1. docs/v3/EXPRESSION.md is the protocol; it specialises docs/v3/CYCLES.md.

change: Follow docs/v3/EXPRESSION.md § The loop for cases n39, n40, n41, n42, n43 and n44 (all native; none has run; n45 stays for cycle 11). Before pinning, check TuffUI (github.com/yurigdesigner/tuffui) for visualization components published after `f31ea2b` (2026-11-16; cycles 7 to 9 found none); for each one, add a `c` case, its reference row and shot (`.evidence/v3-shots/expression-6/ref-shot.ts` in the main checkout shoots a page at 1440x1000 with reduced motion), and run it in place of a native case. With fewer than four referenced cases the cycle file reports the convergence clause on the referenced cases it has and says the clause cannot be met in full; with none, the verdict counts are empty. You are the lead: you spawn, shoot, collect and diagnose; you build nothing and score nothing. (1) Builders: one fresh subagent per case on the default worker tier, with the case row verbatim, the scenario id `expr-<case id>`, and the fence of cycle 9 (its builder prompt, `.evidence/v3-shots/expression-9/builder-prompt.md` in the main checkout, is the model; its lead tools are in the same directory). Pre-register the registry and scenario-info entries with placeholders so each builder owns one directory, run oxfmt on scenario-info.ts after adding them, and tell builders that `fixture` reaches the scenario as a prop. Each builder builds into its own dist directory and shoots its own route. (2) Shoot each scenario with apps/playground/scripts/shots.ts, plus the keyboard frame, the list frame and the pointer sweep of cycle 9's lead tool (`lead-shots.ts` with `shoot-round.sh`). (3) Reviewers: one fresh subagent per case and round, never the builder, with the case row, the shot paths, a snapshot of the scenario source for that round, docs/v3/expression/rubric.md and the shoot log. Tell it to open every shot. (4) Repair: hand the builder its reviewer's findings, at most two more rounds, shooting and scoring after each. (5) Diagnose every point lost in round 0 into one class from EXPRESSION.md § Finding classes, using the builder's wish list and its workaround comments as evidence. Where an open plan row already owns a gap, class the finding `planned` and append it as a `notes` entry to that row's brief instead of filing a row. (6) Judge the three hypotheses against EXPRESSION.md § Thresholds, using this cycle's numbers and the verdict lines of docs/v3/spikes/viz-census.md; for hypothesis 1, say whether cycle 9's kill holds or was a one-cycle result. (7) File per CYCLES.md step 6. A fix that adds a public export, changes charts/contract.ts or changes what primitive-bypass denies is one row with `checkpoint: spec` and seat opus high. Report factory friction with `factory signal file`, not as a row. Lead notes from cycle 9: (a) check v3-expr-9-kit-fixes before round 0 on a build of the pinned master: n34, n35 and n38 at 390 (loading and rest end at one height), n38's top-item label at 390 and 1800, n34's refLine labels at 390, n38 `?fixture=extreme` (the clamped dot shows 41), n37's focused bar among grey bars and n38's dimmed accent dots in dark, n36's phone cards (every value labelled), n33 `?shot-state=empty` and `error` (a full header row); if any did not land, tell builders so the same gap does not cost twice; (b) check v3-expr-9-contract: tell reviewers what the Spec ruled and which fields shipped (a list row that joins a chart's focus across grains, a declared table skeleton row count); (c) check v3-expr-9-rubric: if its two sentences landed, the reviewer reads them from rubric.md; if not, tell reviewers the readings the cycle-9 file records for X3 and X4 on a page with no chart; (d) run `make check-fast` on the round-0 tree before round 1 starts, never while a builder edits: in cycle 9 a round-1 builder's edit landed mid-run and the quality matrix failed on its half-written fixture; (e) keep cycle 9's reviewer notes on the two sanctioned colour forms, the 61 px band, the LIST approach and the shipped series-row, mono, stacked BarList, Sparkline readout and bar value fields; (f) keep the builder prompt's line to look at the page the way the skill's last step says, without naming the keys state, and count who shot a keyboard frame (cycle 9: 6 of 6 in round 0); (g) `demo/series.ts` is shared: tell builders to change only their own group with one Edit after a fresh Read and never to rewrite the file, and to run `bun test` on its own; (h) once this cycle runs, the bank's only never-run cases are n45 and the ones it adds: add at least five from pages no case covers yet, so cycle 11 can draw six, and say so; (i) report every score on all items and, for the trend against cycles 1 and 2, on the F and K items alone, as cycles 3 to 9 do; (j) the lead tool takes a chart's own HTML rows (`[data-chart-mark]`) for a list and a table's `c.meter` cells for sweep marks (cycle 9: n35's day track, n33's and n36's age meters): read each LIST and SWEEP line against its frame and tell the reviewer what it hovered; (k) two cycle-9 cases (n33, n36) were pages of tables and never passed: if a case this cycle is a page with no chart, say in the cycle file whether the rubric's X3 and X4 readings held.
